target_customer: Residential energy efficiency and electrification contractors in the US who must help customers find and apply for rebates, incentives and green financing
problem: Over $80B of rebates, incentives and financing exists for efficiency upgrades but is scattered across utilities, federal funds, grants and green lenders, so contractors and customers struggle to find and claim it.
business_model: B2B SaaS for contractors with an API for quoting tools (pricing not found)
product_category: Climate fintech: incentives and financing software for contractors

founders.name: Stephanie Vasquez
founders.background_notes: YC page: 12+ years building and leading product, operations and analytics teams, with risk and payments experience. Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Dasha Cherepennikova
founders.role: Founder (author of the YC launch post; Crunchbase snippet lists CEO)
founders.background_notes: YC page: 12+ years scaling hard problems through automation and ML, product leader from 0 to 1 and 1 to 100. Education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A directory of incentive programs with application workflows and an API is mostly standard web and data work. The hard part was keeping fragmented, changing program rules current, which is data operations more than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The value rested on aggregated program data and contractor workflow. Other rebate startups reached the same market within months, and program rules are public, so copying was feasible.

incumbents: Contractor quoting and field service software vendors
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later sources (2024) show contractor quoting tools such as EDEN and Contractor Commerce adding rebate support, but no source ties these to Line.Build specifically.

market_need_then: The YC launch post states that more than $80B of rebates and financing existed and was fragmented. The Inflation Reduction Act home energy rebate funding was starting to flow to states in 2023.

branding.domain_note: Uses line.build, a .build top level domain rather than a .com. No purchase history found.

identity.logo: A plain letter L mark per a directory listing (village.ai)

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, community or merch was found. The word Line is generic and searches for it return programming documentation.

outcome_analysis: Line.Build was a three person Summer 2023 company with a reported YC sized pre-seed of about $500K and no later round found. The YC directory lists it as inactive, but no shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, and the website returned HTTP 503 during this research, so the cause of inactivity is not public. The market was crowded by early 2024 with Sealed, Rock Rabbit and Eli Technologies, and federal rebate funding was disrupted in 2025, but no source links either to this company.
notes: Website line.build returned HTTP 503 on fetch. The $500K pre-seed rests on a single database (VCBacked, repeated by Employbl) with no press release. Crunchbase and the YC page disagree with each other on founder titles. No competitor with a source dated at or before the batch was found: the Canary Media article naming Sealed Pro, Rock Rabbit and Eli Technologies is dated 2024-04-01, about seven months after the batch, so none are listed. Competitors list is empty for that reason. Exit type is unknown because the YC status is Inactive but no shutdown source exists.
